common_features: Virtualized navigation, rich sorting/filtering, grouping/aggregation, complete column controls, selection, editing, export, and serializable state.
differentiators: Most complete integrated grid stack: multiple row models, visual Advanced Filter builder, server-side grouping/aggregation, master/detail, integrated charts, sparklines, Excel export, and mature accessibility caveat documentation.
cost_licensing_complexity: High — Community/Enterprise split; per-developer commercial licensing; advanced analytics and row models span paid modules.
implementation_effort: Medium — fast feature coverage, but substantial configuration and design suppression are needed to preserve a calm authored-table UX.
best_fit_use_case: Enterprise analytical workbenches, large remote datasets, and teams that value breadth and vendor support over a minimal abstraction.

common_features: Sorting, filtering, grouping/aggregation, selection, column visibility/order/sizing/pinning, pagination, expansion, and controlled state.
differentiators: Headless, framework-wide architecture with first-party Solid support; complete ownership of markup, progressive disclosure, field profiling, responsive behavior, accessibility, and product-level state.
cost_licensing_complexity: Low — MIT packages with no commercial feature split.
implementation_effort: Large — the table engine is concise, but the complete UX, keyboard model, export, persistence, virtualization, and recovery layers are product code.
best_fit_use_case: Design-led products with unusual field exploration, custom detail surfaces, product-owned view state, and teams willing to build the interaction system.
enterprise_readiness: Medium — high architectural quality, but enterprise controls are application work

common_features: Virtualization, sorting/filtering, column controls, selection, editing, export, state, theming, and server-side data.
differentiators: Strong React-native integration, polished built-in controls, Premium grouping/aggregation/pivot/chart integration, and a documented accessibility target.
cost_licensing_complexity: Medium-high — MIT core plus Pro/Premium feature gates and annual per-developer licensing.
implementation_effort: Medium in React; large if adopting React only for the grid.
best_fit_use_case: React applications already standardized on MUI that need a polished grid and are comfortable with Pro/Premium licensing.

common_features: Virtualized rows, sorting/filtering/grouping, column controls, selection, editing, validation/history, download/export, and state persistence.
differentiators: Mature MIT, framework-neutral, batteries-included grid with a smaller abstraction and lower lock-in than enterprise suites.
implementation_effort: Medium — most mechanics are present; field profiling, polished filter composition, saved-view semantics, and custom detail UX remain.
best_fit_use_case: Framework-neutral applications needing a capable OSS grid without adopting a React-specific ecosystem or an enterprise license.

common_features: Sorting/searching, server-side processing, column visibility/reorder, responsive details, selection, exports, modular filtering, and state persistence.
differentiators: SearchBuilder + SearchPanes + StateRestore provide unusually strong query-building, facets, and named-state UX in a mature DOM-table ecosystem.
cost_licensing_complexity: Medium — MIT core/extensions plus separately licensed Editor.
implementation_effort: Medium — low for classic reporting tables; higher when composing many extensions into one coherent progressive-disclosure UX.
best_fit_use_case: Report-like tables, existing server-rendered/DOM-table applications, and teams that value mature extensions and named state restoration.

common_features: Virtualization, sorting/filtering, complete column manipulation, editing/validation/undo, selection/clipboard, CSV export, persistence, and theming.
differentiators: Spreadsheet-grade editing, formulas, merged cells, clipboard/range interaction, and validation.
cost_licensing_complexity: High — commercial business-use terms and per-developer tiers.
implementation_effort: Medium for spreadsheet UX; large to suppress spreadsheet behavior and replace it with progressive record exploration.
best_fit_use_case: Editable spreadsheet-like applications, financial models, planning tools, and data-entry grids.
open_source_maturity: Low for commercial delivery; mature source code

common_features: Virtualization, sorting/filtering/grouping, full column controls, detail rows, editing, selection, exports, controlled state, and theming.
differentiators: Polished enterprise React suite, advanced filtering, RSC/server patterns, strong support, and broad adjacent components.
cost_licensing_complexity: Medium — free subset plus premium per-developer subscriptions.
implementation_effort: Medium in React; large for a Solid/plain-JS codebase.
best_fit_use_case: React enterprise applications standardized on Progress/Telerik components and support.

common_features: Virtualization, rich filters, grouping/aggregates, full column controls, detail templates, editing/validation, selection, Excel/PDF, state persistence, and themes.
differentiators: Very broad suite, Excel-like filtering, lazy grouping, strong export, multi-framework coverage, and an unusually generous but eligibility-bound Community License.
cost_licensing_complexity: High — commercial suite plus organization-size eligibility rules for the free Community License.
implementation_effort: Medium — broad feature coverage; high integration/testing surface for combined virtualization, detail, and editing modes.
best_fit_use_case: Multi-framework enterprise applications that want one vendor for grids, charts, exports, and adjacent controls.

common_features: Virtual/infinite/server operations, sorting/filtering/grouping/summaries, column controls, master/detail, editing/validation, selection, Excel/PDF, state storage, and themes.
differentiators: Mature visual FilterBuilder, broad remote-data support, current natural-language grid assistant, rich exports, and explicit accessibility caveat documentation.
cost_licensing_complexity: Medium — commercial per-developer subscription; broad suite included.
implementation_effort: Medium — high capability coverage, but product-state adapters and UX simplification remain necessary.
best_fit_use_case: Enterprise CRUD/analytics applications needing multi-framework support, remote operations, strong filtering, and vendor support.

common_features: Sorting/filtering, selection, editing, expansion, column interactions, templating, and CSV-oriented table behavior.
differentiators: Primitive/styled/headless successor architecture and a broad visual component ecosystem, but currently dominated by migration and licensing uncertainty.
cost_licensing_complexity: High — legacy MIT lineage plus new Community eligibility and Commercial keys/pricing.
best_fit_use_case: React teams already committed to the Prime ecosystem and willing to pin a specific successor release/license.

common_features: Sorting/filtering, pagination/virtualization, selection, expandable rows, fixed columns, custom cells, summaries, and editable ProTable workflows.
differentiators: Schema-driven query forms and request lifecycle in ProTable; strong React design-system integration; MIT licensing.
implementation_effort: Medium — fast in Ant applications, but advanced table mechanics and product-owned state remain.
best_fit_use_case: React admin/reporting applications already using Ant Design and needing generated search forms.

common_features: Virtual scrolling, sorting, selection, column controls, hierarchy/details, custom renderers, and app-managed state.
differentiators: Web-component delivery with strong Java Flow integration, lazy data providers, Auto Grid/CRUD generation, and enterprise application tooling.
cost_licensing_complexity: Medium — Apache core plus commercial Grid Pro/platform editions.
implementation_effort: Medium in Vaadin; large relative to the current repo.
best_fit_use_case: Java enterprise applications and teams standardizing on Vaadin’s full-stack platform.

common_features: Virtualized rendering, selection, cell editing, column sizing/freezing, custom cells, and app-controlled state.
differentiators: Canvas throughput, million-row demonstration, and unusually deep custom cell drawing control.
implementation_effort: Large — filtering, grouping, export, persistence, detail, accessibility, and recovery are mostly product code.
best_fit_use_case: React applications where extreme rendering density and custom canvas cells dominate over native semantics and turnkey analytics UX.

common_features: Row/column virtualization, sorting/filtering, column controls, editing, selection, custom cells, and app-controlled persistence.
differentiators: Framework-neutral Web Component, strong two-dimensional virtualization, broad wrapper list, and optional Pro analytics without adopting React.
cost_licensing_complexity: Medium — MIT core plus per-developer Pro tiers.
implementation_effort: Medium-large — grid mechanics are present; higher-order exploration UX and state/recovery remain.
best_fit_use_case: Framework-neutral high-density grids, including Solid-adjacent architectures that want a Web Component and optional paid analytics.

common_features: Virtualized data view, sorting/filtering/grouping/aggregation, configurable columns, exportable/serializable views, and theming.
differentiators: Fast streaming analytic engine, Arrow/WASM/Python stack, pivot/split/aggregate model, and integrated multi-chart plugins.
implementation_effort: Medium for an analytics workspace; large to reshape into the prototype’s authored table.
best_fit_use_case: Streaming analytics, pivot-heavy exploration, notebooks, market/telemetry data, and linked chart-grid workspaces.

common_features: Virtual rendering, rich sort/filter/group/summary, full column controls, detail/nested grids, editing, selection, export, state, and themes.
differentiators: Facet filtering, nested grids, sparklines, broad export formats, polished examples, and strong scheduler-adjacent enterprise ecosystem.
cost_licensing_complexity: Very high — named developer plus SaaS/OEM/customer-organization considerations.
best_fit_use_case: Commercial enterprise grids and applications already using Bryntum’s scheduling/project suite.

common_features: Row/column virtualization, sorting/filtering/grouping, complete column controls, editing, selection, custom cells, export integrations, and app-owned state.
differentiators: Compact mature API, Excel-like filters, CollectionView integration, two-dimensional virtualization, and broad framework wrappers.
cost_licensing_complexity: Very high — developer seats plus hostname/commercial deployment and custom SaaS/OEM terms.
best_fit_use_case: Commercial multi-framework line-of-business applications wanting a compact all-purpose grid and Excel/PDF integration.

common_features: Sorting/filtering, column controls, virtualized/server data, detail drawers, editing/validation, selection/actions, downloads, and platform state.
differentiators: Fastest internal-tool delivery, visual data-source integration, actions/queries, and app-wide composition rather than a standalone component.
cost_licensing_complexity: High — platform plans and user/builder economics rather than a component license.
implementation_effort: Small inside Retool; prohibitive migration/lock-in cost for this standalone prototype.
best_fit_use_case: Internal operations tools where platform speed and integrations outweigh source-level control and embeddability.
